subject: Elasticity & SLO checklist + live capacity demo request
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@quickretail.com>, QuickRetail SRE <sre@quickretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — elasticity/SLO items & asks

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and action items from Redwood's side so we have a clear discovery checklist before the live capacity session: 

What we heard (please correct if I mis-stated):
- Peak traffic: ~500 concurrent inference sessions at peak during promotional windows, typical baseline ~40 qps.
- Workload shape: short bursts (~30–90s) across many sessions, plus ~100 long-lived streaming sessions for cart recommendations (each session streams incremental tokens).
- Latency SLO target: p95 generation latency <= 200 ms for short requests; streaming token latency target <= 120 ms.
- Throughput target: sustain 2,500 tokens/sec aggregate during peak.
- Warm pool expectation: want <60s perceived cold-start for new bursts; prefer some pre-warmed instances for predictable response.

Redwood asks / next steps: 
1) Can you confirm exact concurrency definition — is "500 concurrent sessions" equal to 500 simultaneous model contexts (user sessions) or 500 concurrent HTTP connections?
2) Can you share a representative traffic CSV or a short one-hour trace (timestamps + request size + streaming flag) so we can simulate realistic batching and cache behavior?
3) We'd like to schedule a 60-minute live capacity demo where we: run a replay of a 15-minute peak, show scale-up times with and without warm pool, and validate p95/p99 under two model quantization profiles. Do any of these time slots work for you next week: Wed 5/26 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu 5/27 13:00–14:00 PT?
4) We'll attach a short SLO matrix template and a warm-pool runbook draft for your ops to review.

Attachments: quickretail-slo-matrix.xlsx (stub), redwood-warm-pool-runbook.pdf (stub)

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@quickretail.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: QuickRetail SRE <sre@quickretail.com>, Procurement <procurement@quickretail.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:10:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — elasticity/SLO items & asks

Thanks Marcus — that recap is accurate. A few clarifications from our side: 

- "500 concurrent sessions" = 500 active model contexts / user sessions. Each session maintains a KV cache. Our front-end keeps connections alive; the user-facing HTTP layer collapses to ~400 TCP connections during peak because of connection pooling.
- Streaming sessions: roughly 100 sessions that keep an open stream and receive token batches every 250–600ms for up to 3 minutes. Typical token sizes vary between 20–80 tokens per batch.
- For SLOs we actually care about p95 for the first token (<=200ms) and per-token streaming latency p50/p95 <=120ms/300ms respectively (we're more tolerant of p99 spikes during massive promotional events).
- We can provide a redacted 1-hour trace (CSV) and a small replay harness. I'll route that to you via Google Drive link by EOD.

On the times: Wed 5/26 10:00 PT works best for our engineering and SRE teams.

Also: procurement asked for a rough capacity estimate (ballpark monthly committed GPUs for that target traffic) and an expected incremental cost for warm-pool reservation. Can you include that in the demo materials?

Thanks — Alyssa
Alyssa Chen
Head of Product, QuickRetail
alyssa@quickretail.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@quickretail.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:20:35 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — elasticity/SLO items & asks

Alyssa — thanks for the clarifications. Quick technical plan and a few asks so the demo validates the exact behaviors you care about: 

1) Concurrency vs connections: we'll model 500 active model contexts (KV cache per context) mapped to ~400 active streaming TCP connections in the replay. That matters because kernel memory and KV residency are per-context.

2) Warm pool sizing: for 500 contexts with 100 streaming, 5–8 pre-warmed instances (A100/80GB equivalent) should keep p95 first-token <200ms in our sims; without warm pool we typically see scale-up latencies of 45–120s depending on GPU provisioning and model load. For the demo we'll show both behaviors.

3) Queueing behavior: Redwood's serving runtime enforces a hard concurrency cap per instance to bound latency; excess requests are queued at the routing tier rather than the model process to avoid long tail latencies. For your SLOs we recommend: immediate routing fallback to a lower-capacity variant for non-streaming requests, and a short queue (10–15s) for streaming sessions with prioritized token emission to avoid head-of-line blocking.

4) Testing knobs we'll exercise during the demo:
   - Burst ramp rates: 1s, 10s, 30s ramp to peak
   - Warm pool on/off
   - Prioritized streaming vs batch generation mix (10/90, 30/70)
   - Token batch sizes variability (20–80 tokens)

5) Data we need from you before the session:
   - The 1-hour trace (CSV) you mentioned
   - A sample session payload (so we can validate KV cache warm-hit behavior)

6) Deliverables after the demo:
   - A short runbook with recommended warm-pool size and policy (we'll attach a draft: redwood-warm-pool-runbook.pdf)
   - A proposed SLO matrix filled with measured p50/p95/p99 from the replay and an estimate of committed GPU-months for your expected peak.

I'll attach the initial test-plan (slo-test-plan.yaml) — it contains exact load profiles we'll execute. If procurement wants a line-item estimate, Monica will draft a commit scenario at the 6/12/24 month levels; Monica can you own that?

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
